posts.text: Senator Collins’ (R-ME) NO vote on Clarity was the most surprising today. She was defending the bill to constituents as recently as last week. My guess is she did not believe the bill had a chance to pass, and was more worried about defending a yes vote as her re-election prospects look slimmer.
posts.summary: Suggests Collins voted strategically to protect re-election prospects

congress-legislation.quote: Senator Collins’ (R-ME) NO vote on Clarity was the most surprising today. She was defending the bill to constituents as recently as last week. My guess is she did not believe the bill had a chance to pass, and was more worried about defending a yes vote as her re-election prospects look slimmer.

Senator Tillis (R-NC) just entered a motion to reconsider the vote. While this is an attempt to streamline a reconsideration vote rather than re-filing for cloture, I do not think the bill can pass in this short a timeframe with the lame duck session quickly approaching.

The crypto industry has been trying to convince themselves that Clarity failing to pass doesn’t matter, because SEC and CFTC heads have promised to write new rules for them anyway. They will — and we need to fight that — but those rules do not have the staying power of legislation.

Here's my post on why the ethics provisions alone on this bill were a non-starter. Some Democrats seemed willing to pass the deeply flawed and industry-written bill if the ethics provisions could limit Trump’s grift, but negotiators were unable to find a version that satisfied both Dems and Trump.
Clarity Act has just surpassed 41 NOs in the cloture vote; it will not advance to a full vote. The bill is essentially dead in the water under this Congress.
That was a procedural move by Tillis to be able to enter the motion to reconsider
Gillibrand was a NO, though only after the cloture vote was mathematically unable to pass.
Alsobrooks is a NO — she was one of the Democrats who voted to pass the bill out of Senate Banking.
Have not heard any of the usual pro-crypto suspects on the Dem side voting in favor yet; Slotkin, Cortez-Masto, Blunt Rochester were NOs. Many have yet to vote.
